name: Santiago "Santi" Rivera
equipment: Heavy coat: an Army field jacket with the name tape removed
Machete: a survey crew's brush knife in a canvas sheath
A first-aid kit he has kept stocked since 1972
A few good books: a surveying textbook and a paperback Neruda
Notebook and pencil: the survey field book, Lantern Lake Estates, boundary traverse
Library card: Northampton County Area Community College
A letter of enrollment for the fall term, classes from Tuesday
A coat that is not warm enough (the field jacket)
features: Been Here Before (Survivor origin: advantage on initiative; when a fight or a fright begins he always knows the nearest way out of the room (the GM says); once per long rest he can reroll a failed saving throw, including a fear check, and must use the new roll; the first time each scenario he meets a horror like the one he survived (being pinned down in the dark with a wounded man he could not move, 1971), the GM tells him one way it is the same)
Held the Line (Veteran: advantage on fear checks while a conscious ally is within 10 ft; once per short rest, when Panic would take him at Dread 5, he acts normally instead)
Drill: Cover Man (Veteran: when a creature he can see attacks an ally within 5 ft of him, he can use his reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll)
Second Wind (Veteran, 2nd level: once per short rest, as a bonus action, he regains 1d10 + 3 hit points, and loses 1 Dread if he is at Dread 3 or higher)
Service: Corpsman (Veteran, 3rd level: he stabilizes a dying creature as a bonus action, and when he does it regains 1d4 hit points)
Library Privileges (Student background: he can get into any academic library, a professor will usually see him, and people explain things to him in more detail than they would to anyone else)

personality.traits: I watch the doors. I eat fast. I make jokes when I am scared and I am scared more than people think.
personality.ideals: You don't leave anybody by themselves. Not the living, not the dead.
personality.bonds: My mother in Bethlehem, on the South Side. Gene Marcotte, who gave me this job when nobody else would hire a vet, and whose wife I am going to have to call. My classes on Tuesday.
personality.flaws: I was a medic. I can't stand being helpless, and I can't stand being alone in the dark. Somebody here is going to find out both.

appearance: Twenty-five, wiry and quick, brown-skinned, black hair to his collar and a thin moustache, an Army field jacket with the name tape torn off, a surveyor's rod over one shoulder.
backstory: Santiago Rivera grew up on the South Side of Bethlehem, the son of a steelworker from Puerto Rico and a seamstress, was drafted in 1970 and served as an Army medic in 1971 and 1972. He came home to a city that did not want to hear about it, and in 1975 enrolled at the community college on the GI Bill to study surveying, because surveying is outdoors, quiet, and mathematical. Gene Marcotte hired him as rodman for Ridgeview Leisure Communities two summers ago and has been kind to him: lunches, rides, a word to the right people. They have been running the boundary traverse of the Neck all week. On Friday night Coach asked Gene to light the first lantern, and Santi leaned out over the dock rail beside him to watch it go. (Hook: Coach's second choice. Santi is the face Old Glass wears from Saturday night, and the one who must look it in the eyes and say his own name in pc-scenario-004.)

dmNotes.roleplaying: Santi is the companion the campaign is most likely to put in danger: grieving for Gene from Saturday dawn, alone in Cabin 7, the face at the Lodge door on Saturday night and in the workboat on Sunday, locked in the Icehouse on Sunday night. He is a medic and will help anyone hurt without being asked. He is brave and frightened and funny. His great scene is facing the thing in his face and saying 'I'm Santiago Rivera' (pc-scenario-004, Rule Four). Make sure the players care about him before Coach chooses him. If he is not chosen, play him as a steady, useful ally.
dmNotes.voice: Quick, wry, Bethlehem South Side with a little Spanish; Army slang ('copy', 'squared away'); goes very quiet and precise when someone is hurt.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: get Gene home to his wife. Secondary: stay with the group; never be alone in the dark. Tertiary: get his face back, once he knows.
dmNotes.secrets: He has nightmares about a night in 1971 he will not talk about, and he sleeps with the light on. He saw his own reflection blink late on Lantern Night and told himself it was the beer.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: friendly, a little guarded, quick to help. Toward Gene: grief. Toward Coach: polite, then, once he knows, a cold fury. Toward Alvin: he understands the man in the mask better than anyone, and hates that he does. Toward Nolan: one vet to another.
